pr_title: Corrected duplicate ActorID detection in map editor
pr_body: Fixes #19286 and Closes #17895.  Reworked the code that was in place to detect duplicate ActorIDs.
pr_comments: I have made the requested corrections and pushed to the bleed branch.  Is there anything else I need to do on my end?

I had to do the following changes to make this work properly: https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/commit/b8fc1a5759afb0c424ac664e37df54e2fa9f2f03

My test case was creating an empty map, placing two actors and then decreasing the number of the second actor by one. Without the changes the dupe detection would never work because `ActorX` is always unequal to `actorX`.

I feel like I caused more work than I solved on this, my first real contribution to an open source project.  Apologies for that.  Should I keep trying?

Additionally, is there anything else I need to do to finish this one off?

Thanks.

> I feel like I caused more work than I solved on this, my first real contribution to an open source project. Apologies for that. Should I keep trying?

Don't worry, everyone needs to start somewhere. ^^

> Additionally, is there anything else I need to do to finish this one off?

Adding the changes from https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/commit/b8fc1a5759afb0c424ac664e37df54e2fa9f2f03 into this PR should then cover all cases, unless I missed some other case?

Finally it would be good if you can squash all the commits of the PR before we merge it.

@abcdefg30 - Thank you for the encouragement.  I have somehow managed to screw this up too.  I squashed the existing commits with no trouble (I think).  I couldn't see any obvious way to add your commit, so I just made the changes on my end, tested, checked in and pushed those changes - there is now a new changeset - but now I cannot figure out how to squash those commits together.  I fear I may have screwed something up.  Please let me know what I need to do to fix?

Thanks again.

Can squash with `git rebase upstream/bleed -i`. Mark the commits that aren't the correct one (`d0d3b2f`) with a `d` for drop commit. Then force push the branch.

If you do future PRs, you will likely use `f` for fixup instead of `d`, which will merge changes into the correct existing commit.
Dropped the specified commit, force pushed, now I'm getting merge conflicts?  Seems odd.  I'm not sure how to fix.  Can we ditch this PR and make a new one?  :)
Sorry, I meant drop all commits except for the one I specified.

@Smittytron - Ok, I did that, was able to finish this time.  I'm afraid I don't know enough to tell if it is right now.  Would you please take a look?

Thank you for your help.

I might have misread @abcdefg30's comment thinking b8fc1a5 was meant to replace everything else. If we're just trying to squash everything instead then you just need to `git rebase upstream/bleed -i` and use an `f` for fixup on every commit except the top one.

> Can we ditch this PR and make a new one? :)

If you have trouble with git (which can be quite tricky to use right at times) that is also ok.
I have no idea how to get this back to a sensible state.  Too much work for so few lines of code.  I'm going to close this one and start a new one.

comments: I expect this to be another regression from #17867.

https://resource.openra.net/maps/33981/

this map and all mod map derivated

> 
> 
> https://resource.openra.net/maps/33981/
> 
> this map and all mod map derivated

This map doesn't exist on RC.

The problem is that the map contains two actors with the same id `Actor176`
```
	Actor176: t01
		Owner: Neutral
		Location: 46,34

	Actor176: mpspawn
		Location: 91,48
		Owner: Neutral
```
Possibly related to undo/redo - are we recalculating the actor id when applying the redo action?
Sry about the map being out of RC, I made a "spring" cleaning in my uploads and forgot about this. that is wierd, i don't think i edited this map with a playtest having the undo redo.

Then this have nothing to do with undo redo, only that the symptom is showing. 
The fix is to give one of the actors a unique id.

ok, I'll look into the map and fix my yaml.

Sorry for the inconvenience.

the question is: how did the duplicate id end up in there?

We should also not crash on duplicate id, and instead treat the second one as an override for the first (usual yaml-merging convention).
I disagree. Defining two actors with the same ID is bogus and seeing that this is used for scripting might have unexpected effects. We should crash with a better exception though.

at the very least we should be detecting this error and preventing the map from being used in the lobby, like we do for bogus rules. Malicious players should not be able to crash other people by intentionally starting a game with a bad map.
@teinarss mentioned that they had a PR ready to go for this.

review_comments: Is there a difference between the actors in `world.Map.ActorDefinitions` and `editorActorLayer`? I'd expect them to be the same initially, but only `editorActorLayer` getting updated while working on the map.
Thinking about it, the real error here could only be the missing `!` in front of the first if, or am I missing something else?
I'm very new to all of this, so please bear with me.  What you have said matches my observations.  I don't think I understand your question/concern?
We definitely shouldn't be using `world.Map.ActorDefinitions` here. @abcdefg30 is correct that this is only used during the initial map load and (re)saving.

@chrisharris333 my apologies. To be more clear: I was wondering if just changing `CurrentActor.ID.Equals(actorId, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)` to `!CurrentActor.ID.Equals(actorId, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)` and keeping the `editorActorLayer[actorId] != null` check is enough to fix the issue.
Doesn't work just adding the !.  @pchote Is there a list of actors that does get updated as the map gets worked on?
The `if (editorActorLayer[actorId] != null)` is already doing the right thing here. You just need to make sure that `actorId` is already ToLowered.
Ok, I figured out why it didn't appear to be doing anything.  Stay Tuned.
So it was working as expected, but it just wasn't doing anything.  The few new lines I added do make the "Duplicate ActorID" message actually show up now, with the original detection code.
@abcdefg30 and @pchote please take another look when you get the chance.  Thanks.
